text:
Bank results dominated Monday's close: private banks dragged the benchmarks lower while PSU banks rose.

• Sensex closed at 73,852.90, down 876.37 points (1.17%); Nifty 50 closed at 22,888.95, down 257.21 points (1.11%), per Kotak Neo closing report.
• Bank Nifty closed at 55,488.10, down 355.90 points (0.64%), per Liquide and India IPO (CNBC TV18).
• Axis Bank fell 4.19% after its September-quarter results, per Kotak Neo and Liquide; HDFC Bank also declined after its Q2 FY27 results, per Equitymaster and India IPO.
• Nifty PSU Bank rose about 2%, the only sectoral gainer among the indices cited, per Kotak Neo and India IPO.

Our view: results season tends to separate banks by individual numbers rather than moving the whole sector together, and today's split between private and PSU banks looks consistent with that. One session is a thin sample, so this may be stock-specific reaction rather than a lasting rotation. This is an interpretation, not a prediction or advice.

For practitioners: during results season, how do you separate company-specific moves from sector-wide ones when reading the index?
